# Abstract {.unnumbered} 

## Background

Severe pain following tonsillectomy is common and an important cause of delays to discharge and secondary postoperative complications. Clinical guidelines offer a range of perioperative analgesia recommendations but the optimal intraoperative opioid strategy remains unknown. This study aimed to evaluate existing variation in perioperative analgesic management and its impact on postoperative outcomes at a high-volume surgical centre. 

## Methods

A retrospective cohort study was performed to identify all patients undergoing tonsillectomy, adenoidectomy or combined adenotonsillectomy over a 7-year period using routinely collected data from the electronic patient record. Medication exposure and outcomes were extracted, and patients grouped on analgesic exposure to simple analgesia (paracetamol, dexamethasone and diclofenac), plus or minus additional morphine, fentanyl or both. Descriptive analysis of the analgesic exposure, treatment groups and multilevel modelling was performed. 

## Results

`r comma(nrow(df))` patients were included, of which `r N(df$adult == 0)` (`r P(df$adult == 0)`) were paediatric patients. `r P(adults$simple_analgesia_given)` of adults received all three components of simple analgesia compared to `r P(paeds$simple_analgesia_given)` of paediatric patients. `r P(adults$intra_op_opioid_given)` (n = `r N(adults$intra_op_opioid_given)`) of adult patients and `r P(paeds$intra_op_opioid_given)` (n = `r N(paeds$intra_op_opioid_given)`) of paediatric patients received a strong opioid medication intraoperatively. Whilst paediatric patients were predominantly treated with a fentanyl only opioid strategy, adults demonstrated substantial variation across the treatment strategies.

There was no significant difference in the need for recovery opioids between treatment groups for adult patients, however simple analgesia with both morphine and fentanyl resulted in a reduced time in recovery (`r beta(3, "treatment_arm4")` minutes, 95% CI `r beta(3, "treatment_arm4", "conf.low")` to `r beta(3, "treatment_arm4", "conf.high")`).

## Conclusions

Intraoperative opioid strategies varied for adults undergoing tonsillectomy procedures, but were more homogeneous in paediatric patients. When accounting for patient, surgical and anaesthetic factors, a combined opioid regime of fentanyl and morphine with complete simple analgesia was associated with significantly reduced time in recovery and a non-significant but increased odds ratio of same day discharge admission. Further work to address the limitations of data quality and possible causality is needed to build evidence for intra-operative opioids in tonsillectomy.
